My land is only 1.1 mu, very small. With five people in the house and some working outside, this plot is mostly to keep our own grain bin full and sell a little. I have farmed 30 years so I know what works here in Quzhou.

For winter wheat, I plant in early October after the maize comes off. I use improved seed from the agro-supply shop — Jimai or Shiluan types, whatever the dealer has that the neighbors are using. About 15 kg seed for this plot. Before sowing I spread compound fertilizer, the 15-15-15 kind, maybe one bag (50 kg) as base — that gives me around 7 kg N, 7 kg P, 7 kg K per mu on this little plot. Then at jointing in March I topdress urea, about 15 kg urea per mu, which is roughly 7 kg N more. So total nitrogen around 14 kg/mu. Phosphorus and potassium only in the base. I irrigate from the well — overwinter water in December, jointing water, and grain-filling water, three times. Pesticide twice: once for aphids and powdery mildew around April, and herbicide earlier. I plough before sowing wheat, the soil needs turning after maize stubble. I expect around 450 kg/mu, last year was about that.

For summer maize, I direct seed right after wheat harvest in June, no tillage, just drill into the stubble — everyone does this now, saves time and water. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Denghai type, about 2.5 kg for the plot. Base fertilizer compound 40 kg at sowing, then urea 20 kg/mu at the big trumpet stage. Total N around 18 kg/mu for maize because maize eats more nitrogen than wheat. Irrigate once or twice depending on rain — usually July rains come but if dry I pump once. Pesticide once or twice for armyworm and corn borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

Money is tight so I don't overspend on fertilizer, but I won't skimp either — a bad harvest on 1.1 mu still hurts.
